themes_detail.label: Garbage Collection Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Missed Collection complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK versus 1.1 per week baseline—a 433% increase (z-score: 3.02)—signaling a potential sanitation service breakdown in Mott Haven/Melrose just as winter weather intensifies.
evidence: 6 Missed Collection complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (433% spike, z-score: 3.02)
Spike emerged in most recent reporting period, indicating acute, recent problem rather than chronic issue
Street Sweeping complaints also elevated at 7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.1 baseline (522% increase), suggesting broader sanitation service strain
reporting_angles: Interview residents about uncollected garbage piling up; photograph affected blocks to document conditions
Contact DSNY to determine if staffing shortages, route changes, or vehicle breakdowns are causing the miss—and when service will normalize

themes_detail.label: Unlicensed Cannabis Retailers
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis Retailer complaints exploded to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 0.2 per week baseline—a 1500% spike (z-score: 8.66, severity: high)—indicating possible illegal retail operations or lack of enforcement in the district.
evidence: 4 Cannabis Retailer complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% increase, z-score: 8.66, highest severity flag in dataset)
Spike is statistically extreme and represents the single-largest outlier in 311 data, suggesting cluster of complaints about same issue
Indicates either new illegal operations or sudden community reporting wave about existing problem
reporting_angles: Scout storefronts in Mott Haven/Melrose advertising cannabis; interview neighbors about impact on street conditions or youth access
Request SLA and NYPD enforcement data on unlicensed retailers in CD 201 over past month; ask why complaints spiked suddenly

themes_detail.label: Police Non-Emergency Call Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints jumped to 18 LAST WEEK versus 5.9 per week baseline—a 206% increase (z-score: 5.81)—suggesting a spike in low-level crime, disorder, or community concerns triggering police calls.
evidence: 18 Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.9 weekly average (206% increase, z-score: 5.81)
Second-highest statistical anomaly in dataset; sustained elevation suggests pattern, not one-off incident
Convergence signal: paired with 350% spike in Encampment complaints 3 weeks ago (9 vs. 2.0 baseline), may indicate homeless-related disorder or street activity
reporting_angles: Review NYPD 311 records and CompStat data to determine which police matters spiked (disorderly conduct, loitering, trespassing, etc.); map incident locations
Interview precinct commanders and community leaders about what changed on the ground; speak to residents about perceived safety concerns

themes_detail.label: Lead Exposure Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Lead violation complaints spiked to 3 THREE WEEKS AGO versus 0.5 per week baseline—a 500% increase (z-score: 5.0)—raising alarm about potential lead paint hazards in older housing stock affecting children.
evidence: 3 Lead complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% increase, z-score: 5.0)
Mott Haven/Melrose has aging pre-1978 housing stock with high lead-paint risk; complaint spike suggests either new inspections, renovations disturbing lead paint, or increased testing/reporting
Converges with recurring CB budget request for 'additional building inspectors' (same request year after year), indicating chronic underinspection capacity
reporting_angles: Obtain DOB inspection records for lead violations in CD 201; interview affected families about exposure risks and remediation timelines
Investigate why building inspector staffing remains insufficient per CB budget requests; report on city's lead-safe renovation compliance enforcement

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: For Hire Vehicle complaints increased to 3 LAST WEEK versus 1.2 per week baseline—a 140% increase (z-score: 4.04)—suggesting issues with ride-share congestion, illegal pickups, or traffic violations in the district.
evidence: 3 For Hire Vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average (140% increase, z-score: 4.04)
Spike is recent but lower-severity than top signals; may indicate seasonal uptick or new service area expansion
Mott Haven/Melrose is transit-hub adjacent (near Metro-North, subway); ride-share congestion could interact with existing noise and parking complaints
reporting_angles: Interview residents about ride-share double-parking, idling, and traffic; photograph congestion hotspots
Check TLC complaints and enforcement data for CD 201; ask about driver compliance with traffic and parking rules
